shloka_text: ततस्तु सचिवैः सार्धं षड्भिर्नित्यं बलोद्धतैः । महोदरप्रहस्ताभ्यां मारीचशुकसारणैः ।। 7.14.1 ।।
transliteration: tatastu sacivaiḥ sārdhaṃ ṣaḍbhirnityaṃ baloddhataiḥ | mahodaraprahastābhyāṃ mārīcaśukasāraṇaiḥ || 7.14.1 ||
translation: ततस्तु then, सचिवैः with ministers, सार्धम् together with, षड्भिः six, नित्यम् always, बलोद्धतैः arrogant with strength, महोदरप्रहस्ताभ्याम् by Mahodara and Prahasta, मारीचशुकसारणैः by Maricha, Shuka, and Sarana.
explanation: Then, accompanied by six powerful ministers, including Mahodara, Prahasta, Maricha, Shuka, and Sarana, he proceeded.
comments: Ravana with his ministers marches on Kailasa and gives battle to Kubera's Yakshas -- the rakshasa lords slaughter the host, and Ravana, unharmed by their weapons through Brahma's boon, breaks through -- the doorkeeper Suryabhanu bars his way, but Ravana uproots the gateway and reduces him to ashes, routing the Yakshas.

shloka_text: धूम्राक्षेण च वीरेण नित्यं समरगृध्नुना । वृतः संप्रययौ श्रीमान्क्रोधाल्लोकान्दहन्निव ।। 7.14.2 ।।
transliteration: dhūmrākṣeṇa ca vīreṇa nityaṃ samaragṛdhnunā | vṛtaḥ saṃprayayau śrīmānkrodhāllokāndahanniva || 7.14.2 ||
translation: धूम्राक्षेण by Dhūmrākṣa, च and, वीरेण by the brave one, नित्यम् always, समरगृध्नुना eager for battle, वृतः surrounded, संप्रययौ he set out, श्रीमान् the glorious one, क्रोधात् from anger, लोकान् the worlds, दहन्निव as if burning.
explanation: Accompanied by the brave Dhūmrākṣa, who was always eager for battle, the glorious Ravana set out, as if burning the worlds with his rage.

shloka_text: पुराणि स नदीः शैलान्वनान्युपवनानि च । अतिक्रम्य मुहूर्तेन कैलासं गिरिमागमत् ।। 7.14.3 ।।
transliteration: purāṇi sa nadīḥ śailānvanānyupavanāni ca | atikramya muhūrtena kailāsaṃ girimāgamat || 7.14.3 ||
translation: पुराणि cities, स he, नदीः rivers, शैलान् mountains, वनानि forests, उपवनानि groves, च and, अतिक्रम्य having crossed, मुहूर्तेन in a moment, कैलासम् Kailasa, गिरिम् mountain, आगमत् he reached.
explanation: He swiftly crossed cities, rivers, mountains, forests, and groves, reaching Mount Kailasa in a short time.

shloka_text: सन्निविष्टं गिरौ तस्मिन्राक्षसेन्द्रं निशम्य तु । युद्धे ऽत्यर्थकृतोत्साहं दुरात्मानं समन्त्रिणम् ।। 7.14.4 ।।
transliteration: sanniviṣṭaṃ girau tasminrākṣasendraṃ niśamya tu | yuddhe 'tyarthakṛtotsāhaṃ durātmānaṃ samantriṇam || 7.14.4 ||
translation: सन्निविष्टम् settled, गिरौ on the mountain, तस्मिन् on that, राक्षसेन्द्रम् the lord of Rakshasas, निशम्य having perceived, तु indeed, युद्धे in battle, अत्यर्थकृतोत्साहम् extremely enthusiastic, दुरात्मानम् the evil-minded one, समन्त्रिणम् with his ministers.
explanation: The lord of Rakshasas, Ravana, was perceived to be settled on that mountain with his ministers, an evil-minded one extremely enthusiastic for battle.

shloka_text: यक्षा न शेकुः संस्थातुं प्रमुखे तस्य रक्षसः । राज्ञो भ्रातेति विज्ञाय गता यत्र धनेश्वरः ।। 7.14.5 ।।
transliteration: yakṣā na śekuḥ saṃsthātuṃ pramukhe tasya rakṣasaḥ | rājño bhrāteti vijñāya gatā yatra dhaneśvaraḥ || 7.14.5 ||
translation: यक्षा the Yakṣas, न not, शेकुः were able, संस्थातुं to stand, प्रमुखे in the presence, तस्य of that, रक्षसः Rākṣasa (Ravana), राज्ञो of the king (Kubera), भ्राता brother, इति thus, विज्ञाय having known, गता went, यत्र where, धनेश्वरः the lord of wealth (Kubera).
explanation: The Yakṣas were unable to stand before that Rākṣasa (Ravana), and knowing him to be the king's (Kubera's) brother, they went to where Kubera, the lord of wealth, was.

shloka_text: ते गत्वा सर्वमाचख्युर्भ्रातुस्तस्य चिकीर्षितम् । अनुज्ञाता ययुर्हष्टा युद्धाय धनदेन ते ।। 7.14.6 ।।
transliteration: te gatvā sarvamācakhyurbhrātustasya cikīrṣitam | anujñātā yayurhaṣṭā yuddhāya dhanadena te || 7.14.6 ||
translation: ते they, गत्वा having gone, सर्वम् all, आचख्युर् reported, भ्रातुस् of the brother, तस्य his, चिकीर्षितम् intention, अनुज्ञाता permitted, ययुर् went, हष्टा joyful, युद्धाय for battle, धनदेन by Kubera, ते they.
explanation: Having gone, they reported all of his brother's intentions, and being permitted by Kubera, they joyfully went forth to battle.

shloka_text: ततो बलानां सङ्क्षोभो व्यवर्धत महोदधेः । तस्य नैर्ऋतराजस्य शैलं सञ्चालयन्निव ।। 7.14.7 ।।
transliteration: tato balānāṃ saṅkṣobho vyavardhata mahodadheḥ | tasya nairṛtarājasya śailaṃ sañcālayanniva || 7.14.7 ||
translation: ततो then, बलानां of the armies, सङ्क्षोभो the commotion, व्यवर्धत increased, महोदधेः like the great ocean, तस्य of that, नैर्ऋतराजस्य king of Rākṣasas (Ravana), शैलं a mountain, सञ्चालयन् shaking, इव as if.
explanation: Then, the commotion of the armies of that king of Rākṣasas (Ravana) grew like the great ocean, as if shaking a mountain.

shloka_text: ततो युद्धं समभवद्यक्षराक्षससङ्कुलम् । व्यथिताश्चाभवंस्तत्र सचिवा राक्षसस्य ते ।। 7.14.8 ।।
transliteration: tato yuddhaṃ samabhavadyakṣarākṣasasaṅkulam | vyathitāścābhavaṃstatra sacivā rākṣasasya te || 7.14.8 ||
translation: ततो then, युद्धं a battle, समभवद् occurred, यक्षराक्षससङ्कुलम् crowded with Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, व्यथिताश् distressed, च and, अभवंस् became, तत्र there, सचिवा the ministers, राक्षसस्य of the Rākṣasa (Ravana), ते those.
explanation: Then a battle ensued, crowded with Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, and there the ministers of the Rākṣasa (Ravana) became distressed.

shloka_text: स दृष्ट्वा तादृशं सैन्यं दशग्रीवो निशाचरः । हर्षनादान्बहून्कृत्वा स क्रोधादभ्यधावत ।। 7.14.9 ।।
transliteration: sa dṛṣṭvā tādṛśaṃ sainyaṃ daśagrīvo niśācaraḥ | harṣanādānbahūnkṛtvā sa krodhādabhyadhāvata || 7.14.9 ||
translation: सः He, दृष्ट्वा having seen, तादृशं such a, सैन्यं army, दशग्रीवः Dashagriva, निशाचरः the night-wanderer, हर्षनादान् roars of joy, बहून् many, कृत्वा having made, सः he, क्रोधात् from anger, अभ्यधावत rushed towards.
explanation: Seeing such a vast army, the demon Dashagriva, after uttering many roars of joy, rushed forward in a fit of rage.

shloka_text: ये तु ते राक्षसेन्द्रस्य सचिवा घोरविक्रमाः । तेषां सहस्रमेकैकं यक्षाणां समयोधयन् ।। 7.14.10 ।।
transliteration: ye tu te rākṣasendrasya sacivā ghoravikramāḥ | teṣāṃ sahasramekaikaṃ yakṣāṇāṃ samayodhayan || 7.14.10 ||
translation: ये those, तु indeed, ते those, राक्षसेन्द्रस्य of the king of demons, सचिवाः ministers, घोरविक्रमाः of terrible prowess, तेषां of them, सहस्रम् a thousand, एकैकं each one, यक्षाणां of the Yakshas, समयोधयन् fought.
explanation: Each of those ministers of the king of demons, who were of terrible prowess, fought against a thousand Yakshas.

shloka_text: ततो गदाभिर्मुसलैरसिभिः शक्तितोमरैः । हन्यमानो दशग्रीवस्तत्सैन्यं समगाहत ।। 7.14.11 ।।
transliteration: tato gadābhirmusalairasibhiḥ śaktitomaraiḥ | hanyamāno daśagrīvastatsainyaṃ samagāhata || 7.14.11 ||
translation: ततः then, गदाभिः with maces, मुसलैः with clubs, असिभिः with swords, शक्तितोमरैः with spears and javelins, हन्यमानः being struck, दशग्रीवः Dashagriva, तत् that, सैन्यं army, समगाहत plunged into.
explanation: Then, even while being struck by maces, clubs, swords, spears, and javelins, Dashagriva plunged into that army.

shloka_text: स निरुच्छ्वासवत्तत्र वध्यमानो दशाननः । वर्षद्भिरिव जीमूतैर्धाराभिरवरुध्यत ।। 7.14.12 ।।
transliteration: sa nirucchvāsavattatra vadhyamāno daśānanaḥ | varṣadbhiriva jīmūtairdhārābhiravarudhyata || 7.14.12 ||
translation: सः he, निरुच्छ्वासवत् as if breathless, तत्र there, वध्यमानः being struck down, दशाननः Dashanana, वर्षद्भिः by raining, इव as if, जीमूतैः by clouds, धाराभिः by streams of rain, अवरुध्यत was obstructed.
explanation: There, Dashanana, being struck down as if breathless, was obstructed by the continuous onslaught of weapons, much like clouds pouring down streams of rain.

shloka_text: न चकार व्यथां चैव यक्षशस्त्रैः समाहतः । महीधर इवाम्भोदैर्धाराशतसमुक्षितः ।। 7.14.13 ।।
transliteration: na cakāra vyathāṃ caiva yakṣaśastraiḥ samāhataḥ | mahīdhara ivāmbhodairdhārāśatasamukṣitaḥ || 7.14.13 ||
translation: न not, चकार did he feel, व्यथां pain, च and, एव indeed, यक्षशस्त्रैः by the weapons of the Yakshas, समाहतः struck, महीधरः a mountain, इव like, अम्भोदैः by clouds, धाराशतसमुक्षितः drenched by hundreds of streams of rain.
explanation: Even though struck by the weapons of the Yakshas, he felt no pain, just like a mountain remains unaffected when drenched by hundreds of streams of rain from clouds.

shloka_text: स दुरात्मा समुद्यम्य कालदण्डोपमां गदाम् । प्रविवेश ततः सैन्यं नयन्यक्षान्यमक्षयम् ।। 7.14.14 ।।
transliteration: sa durātmā samudyamya kāladaṇḍopamāṃ gadām | praviveśa tataḥ sainyaṃ nayanyakṣānyamakṣayam || 7.14.14 ||
translation: सः he, दुरात्मा the evil-minded one, समुद्यम्य having raised, कालदण्डोपमां resembling the staff of Yama (Death), गदाम् mace, प्रविवेश entered, ततः then, सैन्यं the army, नयन् leading, यक्षान् the Yakshas, यमक्षयम् to the abode of Yama (death)
explanation: The evil-minded one, having raised his mace resembling the staff of Yama, then entered the army, leading the Yakshas to their death.

shloka_text: स कक्षमिव विस्तीर्णं शुष्केन्धनमिवाकुलम् । वातेनाग्निरिवायत्तो यक्षसैन्यं ददाह तत् ।। 7.14.15 ।।
transliteration: sa kakṣamiva vistīrṇaṃ śuṣkendhanamivākulam | vātenāgnirivāyatto yakṣasainyaṃ dadāha tat || 7.14.15 ||
translation: सः he, कक्षमिव like a dry forest, विस्तीर्णं vast, शुष्केन्धनमिव like dry fuel, आकुलम् crowded/filled, वातेन by the wind, अग्निः fire, इव like, आयत्तः empowered/driven, यक्षसैन्यं the Yaksha army, ददाह burned, तत् that
explanation: He, like a fire empowered by the wind, burned that vast Yaksha army, which was crowded like a dry forest filled with dry fuel.

shloka_text: तैस्तु तत्र महामात्यैर्महोदरशुकादिभिः । अल्पावशेषास्ते यक्षाः कृता वातैरिवाम्बुदाः ।। 7.14.16 ।।
transliteration: taistu tatra mahāmātyairmahodaraśukādibhiḥ | alpāvaśeṣāste yakṣāḥ kṛtā vātairivāmbudāḥ || 7.14.16 ||
translation: तैः by them, तु indeed, तत्र there, महामात्यैः by the great ministers, महोदरशुकादिभिः like Mahodara, Shuka, and others, अल्पावशेषाः few remaining, ते those, यक्षाः Yakshas, कृताः were made, वातैः by winds, इव like, अम्बुदाः clouds
explanation: There, those Yakshas were reduced to a few remaining, like clouds scattered by winds, by those great ministers such as Mahodara and Shuka.

shloka_text: केचित्समाहता भग्नाः पतिताः समरक्षितौ । ओष्ठांश्च दशनैस्तीक्ष्णैरदशन्कुपिता रणे ।। 7.14.17 ।।
transliteration: kecitsamāhatā bhagnāḥ patitāḥ samarakṣitau | oṣṭhāṃśca daśanaistīkṣṇairadaśankupitā raṇe || 7.14.17 ||
translation: केचित् some, समाहताः struck down, भग्नाः broken/defeated, पतिताः fallen, समरक्षितौ on the battlefield, ओष्ठांश्च and their lips, दशनैः with teeth, तीक्ष्णैः sharp, अदशन् bit, कुपिताः enraged, रणे in battle
explanation: Some, struck down and defeated, fell on the battlefield, while others, enraged in battle, bit their lips with sharp teeth.

shloka_text: श्रान्ताश्चान्योन्यमालिङ्ग्य भ्रष्टशस्त्रा रणाजिरे । सीदन्ति च तदा यक्षाः कूला इव जलेन ह ।। 7.14.18 ।।
transliteration: śrāntāścānyonyamāliṅgya bhraṣṭaśastrā raṇājire | sīdanti ca tadā yakṣāḥ kūlā iva jalena ha || 7.14.18 ||
translation: श्रान्ताः exhausted, च and, अन्योन्यम् each other, आलिङ्ग्य embracing, भ्रष्टशस्त्राः with lost weapons, रणाजिरे on the battlefield, सीदन्ति sank/collapsed, च and, तदा then, यक्षाः the Yakshas, कूलाः riverbanks, इव like, जलेन by water, ह indeed
explanation: Exhausted and with their weapons lost, the Yakshas then collapsed on the battlefield, embracing each other, like riverbanks eroded by water.

shloka_text: हतानां गच्छतां स्वर्गं युध्यतां पृथिवीतले । प्रेक्षतामृषिसङ्घानां न बभूवान्तरं दिवि ।। 7.14.19 ।।
transliteration: hatānāṃ gacchatāṃ svargaṃ yudhyatāṃ pṛthivītale | prekṣatāmṛṣisaṅghānāṃ na babhūvāntaraṃ divi || 7.14.19 ||
translation: हतानां of those killed, गच्छतां of those going, स्वर्गं to heaven, युध्यतां of those fighting, पृथिवीतले on the surface of the earth, प्रेक्षताम् of those watching, ऋषिसङ्घानां of the groups of sages, न not, बभूव there was, अन्तरं space, दिवि in the sky.
explanation: There was no space left in the sky due to the multitude of those killed going to heaven, those fighting on earth, and the groups of sages watching.

shloka_text: भग्नांस्तु तान्समालक्ष्य यक्षेन्द्रांस्तु महाबलान् । धनाध्यक्षो महाबाहुः प्रेषयामास यक्षकान् ।। 7.14.20 ।।
transliteration: bhagnāṃstu tānsamālakṣya yakṣendrāṃstu mahābalān | dhanādhyakṣo mahābāhuḥ preṣayāmāsa yakṣakān || 7.14.20 ||
translation: भग्नांस्तु but those defeated, तान् them, समालक्ष्य having seen, यक्षेन्द्रांस्तु and the great Yaksha chiefs, महाबलान् very powerful, धनाध्यक्षो the lord of wealth, महाबाहुः the mighty-armed, प्रेषयामास sent, यक्षकान् other Yakshas.
explanation: Seeing those powerful Yaksha chiefs defeated, the mighty-armed Kubera, the lord of wealth, dispatched other Yakshas.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे राम विस्तीर्णबलवाहनः । प्रेषितो न्यपतद्यक्षो नाम्ना संयोधकण्टकः ।। 7.14.21 ।।
transliteration: etasminnantare rāma vistīrṇabalavāhanaḥ | preṣito nyapatadyakṣo nāmnā saṃyodhakaṇṭakaḥ || 7.14.21 ||
translation: एतस्मिन् in this, अन्तरे interval, राम O Rama, विस्तीर्णबलवाहनः with extensive army and vehicles, प्रेषितो sent, न्यपतत् fell upon, यक्षो a Yaksha, नाम्ना by name, संयोधकण्टकः Samyodhakantaka.
explanation: O Rama, at that very moment, a Yaksha named Samyodhakantaka, sent with a vast army and chariots, attacked.

shloka_text: तेन चक्रेण मारीचो विष्णुनेव रणे हतः । पतितो भूतले शैलात्क्षीणपुण्य इव ग्रहः ।। 7.14.22 ।।
transliteration: tena cakreṇa mārīco viṣṇuneva raṇe hataḥ | patito bhūtale śailātkṣīṇapuṇya iva grahaḥ || 7.14.22 ||
translation: तेन by that, चक्रेण discus, मारीचो Maricha, विष्णुनेव as if by Vishnu, रणे in battle, हतः killed, पतितो fallen, भूतले on the ground, शैलात् from a mountain, क्षीणपुण्य one whose merit is exhausted, इव like, ग्रहः a planet.
explanation: Maricha was struck down in battle by that discus, as if by Vishnu, and fell to the earth like a planet whose merits are exhausted falling from a mountain.

shloka_text: ससञ्ज्ञस्तु मुहूर्तेन स विश्रम्य निशाचरः । तं यक्षं योधयामास स च भग्नः प्रदुद्रुवे ।। 7.14.23 ।।
transliteration: sasañjñastu muhūrtena sa viśramya niśācaraḥ | taṃ yakṣaṃ yodhayāmāsa sa ca bhagnaḥ pradudruve || 7.14.23 ||
translation: ससञ्ज्ञस्तु but having regained consciousness, मुहूर्तेन in a moment, स he, विश्रम्य having rested, निशाचरः the night-wanderer, तं that, यक्षं Yaksha, योधयामास fought, स he, च and, भग्नः defeated, प्रदुद्रुवे fled.
explanation: However, the night-wanderer Maricha regained consciousness in a moment, rested, and then fought that Yaksha, who was subsequently defeated and fled.

shloka_text: ततः काञ्चनचित्राङ्गं वैडूर्यरजसोक्षितम् । मर्यादां प्रतिहाराणां तोरणान्तरमाविशत् ।। 7.14.24 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ kāñcanacitrāṅgaṃ vaiḍūryarajasokṣitam | maryādāṃ pratihārāṇāṃ toraṇāntaramāviśat || 7.14.24 ||
translation: ततः then, काञ्चनचित्राङ्गं whose body was adorned with gold, वैडूर्यरजसोक्षितम् sprinkled with sapphire dust, मर्यादां the boundary, प्रतिहाराणां of the doorkeepers, तोरणान्तरम् inside the archway, आविशत् he entered.
explanation: Then, he entered the archway, which was the boundary of the doorkeepers, adorned with gold and sprinkled with sapphire dust.

shloka_text: तं तु राजन्दशग्रीवं प्रविशन्तं निशाचरम् । सूर्यभानुरिति ख्यातो द्वारपालो न्यवारयत् ।। 7.14.25 ।।
transliteration: taṃ tu rājandaśagrīvaṃ praviśantaṃ niśācaram | sūryabhānuriti khyāto dvārapālo nyavārayat || 7.14.25 ||
translation: तं him, तु indeed, राजन् O King, दशग्रीवं Dashagriva, प्रविशन्तं entering, निशाचरम् the night-wanderer, सूर्यभानुरिति by the name Suryabhanu, ख्यातो known, द्वारपालो the doorkeeper, न्यवारयत् obstructed.
explanation: O King, the doorkeeper known as Suryabhanu obstructed that Dashagriva, the night-wanderer, as he was entering.

shloka_text: स वार्यमाणो यक्षेण प्रविवेश निशाचरः । यदा तु वारितो राम न व्यतिष्ठत्स राक्षसः ।। 7.14.26 ।।
transliteration: sa vāryamāṇo yakṣeṇa praviveśa niśācaraḥ | yadā tu vārito rāma na vyatiṣṭhatsa rākṣasaḥ || 7.14.26 ||
translation: स he, वार्यमाणो being obstructed, यक्षेण by the Yaksha, प्रविवेश entered, निशाचरः the night-wanderer, यदा when, तु but, वारितो obstructed, राम O Rama, न व्यतिष्ठत् did not stop, स that, राक्षसः demon.
explanation: Though obstructed by the Yaksha, the night-wanderer entered, and O Rama, when that demon was stopped, he did not halt.

shloka_text: ततस्तोरणमुत्पाट्य तेन यक्षेण ताडितः । रुधिरं प्रस्रवन्भाति शैलो धातुस्रवैरिव ।। 7.14.27 ।।
transliteration: tatastoraṇamutpāṭya tena yakṣeṇa tāḍitaḥ | rudhiraṃ prasravanbhāti śailo dhātusravairiva || 7.14.27 ||
translation: ततः then, तोरणम् the archway, उत्पाट्य having uprooted, तेन by that, यक्षेण Yaksha, ताडितः struck, रुधिरं blood, प्रस्रवन् flowing, भाति appears, शैलो a mountain, धातुस्रवैरिव like streams of minerals.
explanation: Then, having uprooted the archway, he was struck by that Yaksha, and with blood flowing, he appeared like a mountain with streams of minerals.

shloka_text: स शैलशिखराभेण तोरणेन समाहतः । जगाम न क्षतिं वीरो वरदानात्स्वयम्भुवः ।। 7.14.28 ।।
transliteration: sa śailaśikharābheṇa toraṇena samāhataḥ | jagāma na kṣatiṃ vīro varadānātsvayambhuvaḥ || 7.14.28 ||
translation: स he, शैलशिखराभेण resembling a mountain peak, तोरणेन by the archway, समाहतः struck, जगाम न did not suffer, क्षतिं harm, वीरो the hero, वरदानात् due to the boon, स्वयम्भुवः of Svayambhu (Brahma).
explanation: Though struck by the archway resembling a mountain peak, the hero suffered no harm due to the boon granted by Svayambhu (Brahma).

shloka_text: तेनैव तोरणेनाथ यक्षस्तेनाभिताडितः । नादृश्यत तदा यक्षो भस्मीकृततनुस्तदा ।। 7.14.29 ।।
transliteration: tenaiva toraṇenātha yakṣastenābhitāḍitaḥ | nādṛśyata tadā yakṣo bhasmīkṛtatanustadā || 7.14.29 ||
translation: तेनैव by that very, तोरणेन by the archway, अथ then, यक्षः the Yaksha, तेन by him, अभिताडितः struck, न not, अदृश्यत was seen, तदा then, यक्षः the Yaksha, भस्मीकृततनुः having his body turned to ashes, तदा then.
explanation: The Yaksha, struck by Ravana with that very archway, was then not seen, his body having been reduced to ashes.

shloka_text: ततः प्रदुद्रुवुः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा रक्षःपराक्रमम् । ततो नदीर्गुहाश्चैव विविशुर्भयपीडिताः । त्यक्तप्रहरणाः श्रान्ता विवर्णवदनास्तदा ।। 7.14.30 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ pradudruvuḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā rakṣaḥparākramam | tato nadīrguhāścaiva viviśurbhayapīḍitāḥ | tyaktapraharaṇāḥ śrāntā vivarṇavadanāstadā || 7.14.30 ||
translation: ततः then, प्रदुद्रुवुः fled, सर्वे all, दृष्ट्वा having seen, रक्षःपराक्रमम् the prowess of the Rakshasa, ततः then, नदीः into rivers, गुहाः into caves, च and, एव indeed, विविशुः they entered, भयपीडिताः afflicted by fear, त्यक्तप्रहरणाः having abandoned their weapons, श्रान्ताः exhausted, विवर्णवदनाः with pale faces, तदा then.
explanation: Then, all of them fled, having witnessed the Rakshasa's prowess, and, afflicted by fear, exhausted, with pale faces, and having abandoned their weapons, they then entered rivers and caves. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुर्दशः सर्गः ।। 14 ।। Thus ends the fourteenth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
